nodes.name: Electroless Ni plating on CC
nodes.procedure: A piece of CC substrate was immersed in an aqueous solution of PdCl2 (20 ppm) and polyvinyl pyrrolidone (PVP, 1 wt%) for 24 h, and then soaked in 1 M NaBH4 solution for 10 min to reduce PdCl2 to Pd catalysts. After cleaning with deionized water, the CC substrate coated with Pd catalysts was placed in the electroless plating solution of NiCl2·6H2O (1.74 wt%), Na3C6H5O7·2H2O (1.72 wt%), NaH2PO2·H2O (1.72 wt%), NH4Cl (0.52 wt%), H3BO3 (0.08 wt%), NH3·H2O (0.16 wt%), and deionized water (94.06 wt%) at 60°C for 60 min. After plating, the Ni/CC substrate was cleaned with deionized water and allowed to dry in air.
nodes.source_text: 2.1. Pretreatment of the substrates... Carbon cloth coated with nickel layers (Ni/CC) was prepared through an electroless nickel plating approach

nodes.name: Spontaneous PBA growth on metal substrates
nodes.procedure: Clean metal substrates including Ni, Co, SLS, Mo, W, Ti, and Ta were directly immersed into a 50 mL aqueous solution of 0.5 mM Fe(NO3)3, 1 mM K3[Fe(CN)6], and 6 mM H2SO4 for 24 h at 25°C. For Ni/CC substrates, the immersion time was shortened to 2 h under the same other conditions. As-prepared PBA-coated substrates were washed thoroughly for several times with deionized water and allowed to dry in air.
nodes.source_text: 2.2. Preparation of PBA coatings on metal substrates... Clean metal substrates including Ni, Co, SLS, Mo, W, Ti, and Ta were directly immersed

nodes.name: Phosphidation of PBA/Ni/CC
nodes.procedure: According to the phosphidation method reported in our previous work, a piece of as-prepared PBA/Ni/CC sample was placed on the top of a ceramic crucible with 0.5 g of red phosphorus powder at the bottom. Then the covered crucible with the samples was annealed under Ar atmosphere (99.99%) at 500°C for 2 h with a heating rate of 5°C min⁻¹. After cooling to the room temperature, the NiFeP/CC substrate was washed thoroughly with deionized water.
nodes.source_text: 2.4. Preparation of the NiFeP/CC... annealed under Ar atmosphere (99.99%) at 500°C for 2 h

nodes.name: Electrodeposition of PBA seeds on FTO
nodes.procedure: The typical electrodeposition was performed at -0.2 V (vs. Hg/Hg2Cl2) for 300 s in a traditional three-electrode system with an FTO substrate as the working electrode, Pt sheet as the counter electrode, and Hg/Hg2Cl2 (Sat.) as the reference electrode. The electrolyte is a mixed solution of 0.5 mM Fe(NO3)3, 0.5 mM K3[Fe(CN)6], 0.1 M KCl, and 12.5 mM H2SO4.
nodes.source_text: 2.3. Preparation of PBA coatings on non-metallic conductive substrates... The typical electrodeposition was performed at -0.2 V (vs. Hg/Hg2Cl2) for 300 s

nodes.name: Epitaxial PBA growth on seeded FTO
nodes.procedure: Subsequently, the FTO substrate deposited with PBA seeds was immersed in the same solution for 24 h for further epitaxial growth of the PB coatings. As-prepared PB/FTO substrate was rinsed thoroughly with deionized water for several times and allowed to dry in air.
nodes.source_text: 2.3. Preparation of PBA coatings on non-metallic conductive substrates... immersed in the same solution for 24 h for further epitaxial growth

nodes.characterization_summary: All PBA coatings including PBA/SLS and PBA/Ni/CC show uniform dense layers; PBA/Ni/CC and PBA/SLS have micrometer-sized particles on top surfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Low-magnification SEM images in Fig. S1 indicate that all the conductive substrates are coated by uniform and dense PBA layers. Many micrometer-sized particles are supported on the top surfaces of the coated substrates for Ni, Co, SLS, and Ni/CC...

nodes.characterization_summary: PBA/SLS shows porous structure with pore sizes tens to hundreds of nm, thickness ~1 μm, composed of PBA nanoparticles; dense layer 80-100 nm thick adhered to SLS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Low-magnification TEM images in Fig. 5a and 5b indicate that the PBA layer grown on the substrate has a porous structure... thickness is about 1 μm.

nodes.characterization_summary: PBA/SLS coating composed of amorphous structures and a few tiny PBA nanocrystals.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM (HRTEM) in Fig. 5d indicates that the layer is composed of amorphous structures and a few tiny PBA nanocrystals.

nodes.characterization_summary: Homogeneous distribution of Fe, N, C elements in PBA/SLS coating; small amount of Cr from SLS substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) element mapping images shown in Fig. 5e-5h illustrate the homogeneous distribution of Fe, N, and C elements.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeP/CC structures contain Ni, Fe, P, O, C; smooth parts high Ni, porous nanosheets high P.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDS measurements are carried out on these two structures... the smooth parts possess a relatively high Ni content... porous nanosheet structures have a high P content.

nodes.characterization_summary: PBA/substrate samples show no apparent PBA diffraction peaks; PBA/Ni/CC shows KNi[Fe(CN)6] peaks at 17.6°, 25.1°, 29.3°, 30.9°, 35.6°; NiFeP/CC shows Fe2P, Ni5P4, NiP2, Ni2P phases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD patterns in Fig. S3 show no apparent diffraction peaks attributed to PBAs... After the phosphidation reaction... ascribed to Fe2P (JCPDS No. 85-1727), Ni5P4 (JCPDS No. 18-0883), NiP2 (JCPDS No. 21-0590), and Ni2P (JCPDS No. 03-0953).

nodes.characterization_summary: PBA coatings show C≡N stretching at 2109, 2158 cm⁻¹; metal-CN deformation at 270 cm⁻¹, stretching at 537, 595 cm⁻¹; NiFeP/CC shows Ni-P, Fe-P peaks at 290, 314, 368 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The apparent Raman shift peaks at around 2109 and 2158 cm⁻¹ in all the samples are fingerprints of the C=N stretching vibration band... Raman spectrum of the NiFeP/CC... four obvious peaks located at 290, 314, 368, and 453 cm⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: PBA/SLS shows Fe 2p peaks at 708.5, 721.5 eV (FeII-[Fe(CN)6]4-), 712.7, 725.3 eV (FeIII-PB); N 1s at 397.7, 399.2, 402.3 eV and C 1s at 284.7 eV confirm C≡N. NiFeP/CC shows Ni 2p at 854.1 (Ni-P), 856.7 eV (Ni-O); Fe 2p at 706.4 eV (Fe-P); P 2p at 129.2, 129.9 eV (M-P).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Fe 2p spectrum in Fig. 4c, two characteristic peaks at 708.5 and 721.5 eV can be assigned to the FeII of the [Fe(CN)6]4- species... The P 2p XPS spectrum in Fig. 7d shows a pair of peaks located at 129.2 and 129.9 eV.
